approach-retain-and-refine-source-regexe.reason: Adding more text patterns preserves a second, unsound rejection authority that cannot distinguish syntax from prose or reliably cover import forms. The existing AST stage is the semantic control and can be proven directly by bounded disposable-copy mutations.

evidence_ids: R1 through R6 each name the AST diagnostic class, artifact, and offending global or specifier before and after source-scan retirement
comment and string-literal controls pass only after raw text matching is removed
generated transport.generated.cjs passes before and fails after the complete-tree filename check with no platform-coupling diagnostic
unmutated disposable package passes and preserves the authored and generated coupling inventory
canonical scope, verification, generated-drift, package, contract, and matrix gates pass without policy, dependency, contract, or public API changes
the #169 command helper has no caller before deletion and the complete verification suite passes after its removal

security_justification.audit_integrity: The change preserves explicit scope-boundary rejection for executable host coupling while eliminating raw-text false positives that make verification evidence misleading.
security_justification.authentication_or_authorization: No identity input, authentication mechanism, privilege decision, or authorization grant changes; the affected checker remains a repository verification boundary.
security_justification.authority_provenance: The AST policy remains the sole authority for classifying authored and generated runtime couplings; no ambient source text is treated as proof of a forbidden integration.
security_justification.concurrency: The scope command remains a single-process static inspection with no shared mutable state, asynchronous scheduling, or ordering behavior added.
security_justification.confidentiality: The checker continues to emit bounded artifact and identifier diagnostics and the controls assert that source markers do not leak into failures.
security_justification.cryptography: No cryptographic primitive, hash, signature, key material, or trust assumption is added or changed.
security_justification.error_disclosure: Replacement controls assert stable diagnostic class, artifact, and detail while keeping source content and absolute fixture paths out of output.
security_justification.external_security_integration: The patch adds no network call, exporter, collector, SIEM, telemetry, browser integration, or external security service.
security_justification.fail_posture: Executable forbidden globals and specifiers continue to fail closed through the AST stage; unreadable artifacts remain fail-closed; only comments and string literals become permitted.
security_justification.lifecycle: No SDK lifecycle, initialization, shutdown, delivery, queueing, retry, or persistence behavior changes.
security_justification.mutation_ownership: Only the scope checker and its disposable verification fixtures change; the #169 rider removes a sole dead helper without changing fixture ownership or runtime behavior.
security_justification.privacy_transformation: No event, client, browser, device, real-user, or personal data is collected, transformed, retained, or exposed.
security_justification.resource_retention: The command retains no data beyond its bounded in-process source-tree and diagnostic collections, and this deletion adds no cache or durable resource.
security_justification.retry_or_redelivery: The scope checker has no retry, redelivery, transport, queue, or delivery semantics, and none are introduced.
security_justification.trust_boundary: The change narrows an unsound text-based trust signal to the established AST and filename controls without admitting a new trusted input or runtime dependency.
